new_packages.label: רָשָׁע כְּצוֹפֶה וּמַחֲלֹקֶת כְּמִכְסֶה
new_packages.label_en: The Wicked as Watchman and Controversy as Covering

bechina_edges_required.basis: הָרָשָׁע הוּא כְּמוֹ צוֹפֶה... כֵּן הָרָשָׁע הוּא שׁוֹמֵר

new_packages.justification: Three bechina equations from the source text form one connected component: רָשָׁע ↔ צוֹפֶה, מַחֲלֹקֶת ↔ מִכְסֶה, and צוֹפֶה ↔ מִכְסֶה. The shared pivot node צוֹפֶה bridges the first interpretation's watchman-cluster to the second interpretation's covering-cluster, producing a single unified package. All five nodes share the same essential nature: they are all forms of external opposition that function, at their root, as a covering/guarding structure — protection-through-concealment. The neutral polarity reflects that these concepts (wicked, controversy, covering) are not inherently aligned with holiness or evil, but function as a structural mechanism whose moral valence depends on degree.

observations:
Torah #208 contains three explicit bechina declarations that form one connected component with five nodes, justifying the proposal of one new package.

The three bechina equations are:
1. רָשָׁע ↔ צוֹפֶה (the wicked IS the city-watchman) — first interpretation, lines 1-2. Language: 'הָרָשָׁע הוּא כְּמוֹ צוֹפֶה... כֵּן הָרָשָׁע הוּא שׁוֹמֵר.' This is the strongest bechina identification — the Rebbe uses the copula הוּא twice to equate the concepts.

2. מַחֲלֹקֶת ↔ מִכְסֶה (controversy IS a covering) — second interpretation, line 3. Language: 'הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת הִיא כְּמוֹ מִכְסֶה לָהֶם.' Clear bechina statement with הִיא כְּמוֹ.

3. צוֹפֶה ↔ מִכְסֶה (the word tzofeh means covering) — second interpretation, line 4. Language: 'צוֹפֶה לְשׁוֹן מִכְסֶה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: וְצִפִּיתָ אוֹתוֹ זָהָב.' This is a linguistic bechina — the Rebbe demonstrates that the root צ-פ-ה carries the meaning of covering (using Exodus 25:11 as proof). In Rebbe Nachman's methodology, establishing that two words share the same root/meaning is a form of bechina: they are different surfaces of the same conceptual-spiritual reality.

The third bechina (צוֹפֶה = מִכְסֶה) is the structural hinge: it unites the first interpretation (where the רָשָׁע is the צוֹפֶה/watchman) with the second interpretation (where מַחֲלֹקֶת is the מִכְסֶה/covering) into one teaching. Without Bechina 3, the two interpretations would be separate conceptual clusters. With it, they collapse into one truth: whether described as 'watchman' or 'covering,' the wicked/controversy performs the same essential function — it is a providentially arranged protective structure around the tzaddik.

The five-node package is the minimum required to represent this teaching's bechina architecture. The eitza relationships (persecution → tzaddik examines deeds; small controversy → protection; excess controversy → seeking to kill) run between and beyond this package and would be represented as directed eitza edges in the graph, not as part of the bechina package itself.

Note: There is no evil-mirror package in this Torah. The standard good/evil polarity structure (e.g., Torah #1's מלכות דקדושה vs. מלכות הרשעה) is absent here. Instead, Torah #208 presents a single paradoxical insight about how apparent evil (the wicked, controversy) is itself, in its essential function, a form of protection — making the polarity assignment neutral rather than the conventional good/evil dichotomy. The absence of an evil mirror is itself structurally significant: the Rebbe is not saying there is a good controversy and an evil controversy; he is saying that all controversy, in small measure, has the nature of a protective covering (though excess of it becomes destructive, as the eitza flow shows).
